messages:
liam: Hey team — I just got my year-end packet and I'm seeing both a 1099-NEC for 2026 and a W-2 for the same periods. On top of that, payroll withheld federal tax on the W-2 payments and Finance applied backup withholding on my contractor invoices (INV-2026-334). I converted from contractor->employee on 2026-07-01. Can someone explain why I'm getting duplicate reporting/withholding?
hr_payroll: Hi @liam — thanks for flagging. Please DM copies of the 1099, W-2, and any invoices/payments (no SSN in chat). We'll triage with Payroll Ops and Tax.
liam: DM'ing the 1099 & W-2 now plus invoice INV-2026-334 and vendor onboarding docs.
payroll-bot: Payroll batch #202607 processed for 2026-07-31; year-end packets generated.
payroll_ops: Quick read: two likely causes — (1) contractor vendor payments were processed through AP earlier in the year and flagged for backup withholding due to missing tax docs, generating 1099 with backup withheld; (2) after conversion on 2026-07-01 pay then ran through the payroll engine producing W-2 wages. If AP and Payroll didn't coordinate removal of vendor profile, both systems could have reported. We'll need to map dates and payment IDs.
finance_ops: Confirming — if backup withholding was applied in error and those payments should've been payroll wages, we need to: 1) reverse any backup withholding and refund the employee 2) correct reporting (issue corrected 1099 or reclassify) 3) consider if employee owes any additional tax because of timing. Tax should advise on reporting path.
tax-team: Flagging requirements: if amounts were already reported on 1099 and W-2, we may need to issue corrected 1099 (1099-NEC) and a W-2c in certain cases, or prepare explanation letters for the employee's tax filing. Backup withholding amounts withheld to the IRS require a refund to the employee and amended reporting. We need exact payment dates and AP remittance IDs.
liam: AP payment refs are AP-8421 (paid 2026-03-15) and AP-8709 (paid 2026-05-10). Both are before conversion. Only payroll payments after 2026-07-01 should be W-2.
hr_payroll: Good detail. Plan: 1) Payroll Ops + AP will crosswalk AP remittances vs payroll wages 2) If AP backup withholding was inappropriate, Finance will issue reimbursement for withheld amount via payroll supplement and request AP correct remittance records 3) Tax team will draft corrective reporting steps. We'll update you in 5 business days.
payroll_ops: Action item: we'll pull payment logs and vendor profile status. If the vendor record wasn't terminated at conversion, AP may have continued to pay through vendor. We'll also confirm whether backup withholding code was applied due to missing W-9.
finance_ops: If reimbursing, we'll aim to process as a payroll adjustment (so it's on W-2) unless Tax advises otherwise. If the backup withholding was transmitted to IRS, we will coordinate refund and filing adjustments.
liam: Appreciate it. One ask — if there's an employee-facing explanation document / letter for my tax preparer that would help.
tax-team: We'll prepare a summary letter and include any corrected form references (e.g., corrected 1099-NEC or W-2c) once we confirm.
payroll-bot: Ticket #PAY-2026-221 created: "Investigate duplicate 1099 + W-2 from contractor->employee conversion" (linked to thread 1791234567). Sensitive docs stored in People Ops secure bucket.
hr_payroll: Liam — please confirm your current payroll ID and vendor ID in the DM so we can reconcile system records.
liam: Sent payroll ID PR-443 and vendor ID V-229.
payroll_ops: Thanks — we're on it. Expect an interim update in 3 business days and a resolution plan within 7 business days.
liam: Thanks everyone — less worried knowing there's a path forward :relieved:
